The leftmost square has 10 written in it, the rightmost square has 130 written in it, and the 3 consecutive squares in the middle are empty. Then reason: Let the three empty squares from left to right be x, y, z respectively, where y is the middle square to be found. According to the problem statement, the sum of the first 3 numbers is 100, so 10 + x + y = 100. The sum of the middle 3 numbers is 200, so x + y + z = 200. Subtract the second equation from the third equation to get 130 - x = 100, therefore x = 30. Substitute x = 30 into 10 + x + y = 100 to get 10 + 30 + y = 100, so y = 60.
